dialogue.content: こんばんは。本日、20:30からよろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Good evening. I look forward to our session from 8:30 PM today.

dialogue.content: 宜しくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Thank you, I look forward to it as well.

dialogue.content: もし準備が整っているようでしたらスタートさせていただいても宜しいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: If you are ready, may we begin?

dialogue.content: はい、スタートしても大丈夫です
dialogue.English: Yes, it's fine to start.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。ではスタートさせていただきます。よろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Thank you. Let's begin then. I look forward to speaking with you.

dialogue.content: こんばんは。相談員です。本日はご相談にきていただきましてありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Good evening. I'm your counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me today.

dialogue.content: 本日はご相談にきていただきましてありがとうございます。相談員です。よろしくお願い致します。
dialogue.English: Thank you for coming to consult with me today. I'm the counselor. I look forward to our session.

dialogue.content: 今日のご相談はどのようなお悩みでしょうか？
dialogue.English: What concerns bring you here today?

dialogue.content: よろしくお願いします
dialogue.English: Thank you for seeing me.

dialogue.content: よろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: You're very welcome.

dialogue.content: 母の事で悩んでいます
dialogue.English: I'm worried about my mother.

dialogue.content: お母さまのことですね。詳しく教えていただけますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: About your mother, I see. Could you please tell me more?

dialogue.content: はい、父も少し関係しているのかもなのですが、
dialogue.English: Yes, and my father might be somewhat involved as well.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 母が交通事故を起こしてから寝たままで起きて来なくなったんです
dialogue.English: Ever since my mother had a car accident, she's been staying in bed and won't get up.

dialogue.content: たまに起きてきては、ぼーっとして
dialogue.English: When she does occasionally get up, she just seems dazed.

dialogue.content: それは、とてもお辛いですね。
dialogue.English: That must be very difficult for you.

dialogue.content: うつろで覇気が無くて
dialogue.English: She's listless and has no energy.

dialogue.content: ええ、そのような状態だととても気がかりだと思います。
dialogue.English: Yes, I imagine it must be very worrying to see her in that state.

dialogue.content: 何を話しかけても、返事をしないで、直ぐ布団に入ってしまいます
dialogue.English: No matter what I say to her, she doesn't respond and just goes right back to bed.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そうですか、そんなお母さまの姿を見ると本当に辛いくて心配ですね。
dialogue.English: I see. It must be truly painful and worrisome to see your mother like that.

dialogue.content: はい。症状が、おかしいんです
dialogue.English: Yes. Her symptoms are strange.

dialogue.content: はい、事故の影響で体の怪我とかは大丈夫なのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. In terms of physical injuries from the accident, is she all right?

dialogue.content: 突然倒れたり
dialogue.English: She suddenly collapses.

dialogue.content: ええ、突然、、それは怖いですね。
dialogue.English: Oh, suddenly... that must be frightening.

dialogue.content: 目に見える体のケガは大丈夫なんです
dialogue.English: There are no visible physical injuries.

dialogue.content: 死にたいと言ったり
dialogue.English: She says things like she wants to die.

dialogue.content: 目に見える怪我は大丈夫でも、そんな症状があると目に見えない分とても心配ですね
dialogue.English: Even if there are no visible injuries, having symptoms like that must be very concerning, especially because you can't see the cause.

dialogue.content: そんな事を、、
dialogue.English: For her to say such things…

dialogue.content: それはあなたやお父様も気が気ではないはずです。
dialogue.English: You and your father must be constantly worried.

dialogue.content: 最近では茶碗を持つ手がガタガタ震えて
dialogue.English: Lately, her hands tremble badly when she holds a bowl.

dialogue.content: 顔は能面で
dialogue.English: Her face is expressionless, like a Noh mask.

dialogue.content: そんな状態で、、毎日、気が休まらないですね。
dialogue.English: In that condition... you must not get a moment's peace.

dialogue.content: はい、失禁もします
dialogue.English: Yes, and she's also become incontinent.

dialogue.content: ええ、ええその症状は病院ではどのように診察されているのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I see. What has the hospital diagnosed regarding these symptoms?

dialogue.content: 廃用症候群だとか、パーキンソン様症候群とか、後、
dialogue.English: They've mentioned disuse syndrome, Parkinsonism, and also...

dialogue.content: 初老認知症だとか、
dialogue.English: Early-onset dementia, and so on.

dialogue.content: 全て、疑いなんです
dialogue.English: But they're all just suspicions.

dialogue.content: はっきりとした病名はないので
dialogue.English: There is no definitive diagnosis.

dialogue.content: 治療できないと言われました
dialogue.English: They told us they can't treat her.

dialogue.content: 脳に異常が見当たらないけど、
dialogue.English: They can't find anything wrong with her brain, but...

dialogue.content: どの病名も心配な病名で、しかも疑いとは、、家族は何とかしたいと考えますよね。
dialogue.English: All of those are worrying diagnoses, and for them to just be suspicions... a family would naturally want to do something.

dialogue.content: はい続けてくださいね
dialogue.English: Yes, please continue.

dialogue.content: このような名前の症状が出てるってだけで
dialogue.English: They just say she's exhibiting symptoms with these names.

dialogue.content: 薬も出るけど、治療としては進まず
dialogue.English: They prescribe medications, but treatment doesn’t progress.

dialogue.content: 段々ひどくなる一方で
dialogue.English: She's just getting worse and worse.

dialogue.content: もう、目の前が真っ暗です
dialogue.English: I feel utterly hopeless.

dialogue.content: ええ、それは心配で何とかしたいお気持ちで、苦しいですね。
dialogue.English: Yes, it must be painful to feel so worried and want to do something but not be able to.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 先ほど、お父様が関係してるかもとありましたが、
dialogue.English: Earlier you mentioned your father might be involved.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そのあたりは何か気がかりでもあるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Is there something concerning in that regard?

dialogue.content: 父が母はただ、怠けてるだけだと、いつも
dialogue.English: My father always says my mother is just being lazy.

dialogue.content: どうして、そんな事を、、
dialogue.English: Why would he say such things…

dialogue.content: 怒鳴りつけて、気合で何とかしようと
dialogue.English: He yells at her, trying to make her snap out of it with sheer willpower.

dialogue.content: いつもしんどい言葉を投げかけ
dialogue.English: He's always saying harsh things to her.

dialogue.content: ええ、いつも、、それは悲しいです
dialogue.English: I see… to have that happen all the time is heartbreaking.

dialogue.content: 対照的で、その仲を保つのが、中々しんどくて
dialogue.English: It's such a contrast, and it's quite draining to try and keep the peace between them.

dialogue.content: あなたはそれをずっとそばで見てこられていたのですね。
dialogue.English: You've been watching this happen all along, haven't you?

dialogue.content: それは、見ていてとても辛いし、しんどいはずです。
dialogue.English: That must be very painful and exhausting to witness.

dialogue.content: はい、今、まだ、生後八か月の子を育てているので
dialogue.English: Yes, and I'm also raising an eight-month-old baby right now.

dialogue.content: ええ
dialogue.English: I understand.

dialogue.content: ハイハイしかけのわが子を連れて病院ばかり通ってます
dialogue.English: I'm constantly going to hospitals with my baby, who is just starting to crawl.

dialogue.content: 母の
dialogue.English: For my mother.

dialogue.content: 更年期の病院に相談すると
dialogue.English: When I consult the clinic for menopausal issues,

dialogue.content: てんかんの気があるからと、また薬が増え
dialogue.English: they said she might have signs of epilepsy and added more medication.

dialogue.content: ええ、また疑い、ということなのですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so it's another suspicion.

dialogue.content: 母が殺されるんじゃないかと思うくらいです。最近はよだれも出てきたので
dialogue.English: It's gotten to the point where I feel like the medications are killing her. She's even started drooling recently.

dialogue.content: そうなんです・・脳外科へ行っても異状ないって
dialogue.English: That's right... even when we went to a neurosurgeon, they said there was nothing wrong.

dialogue.content: 帰されました
dialogue.English: We were just sent home.

dialogue.content: それだけ多くの症状でとても深刻で病院でも原因がわからず、、
dialogue.English: So many serious symptoms, and yet the hospital can't find the cause...

dialogue.content: どうしたらいいのかそんな思いですよね。
dialogue.English: You must be feeling at a loss for what to do.

dialogue.content: あなたも産後や子育てで一番大変な時で自分とお子さんの事で精一杯なのに、、
dialogue.English: And you're in the most difficult period of postpartum and child-rearing, with your hands full just taking care of yourself and your child.

dialogue.content: もう、このまま死んでいくんじゃないかって毎日泊まってるんですが
dialogue.English: I'm so worried she's just going to die like this that I've been staying over every night.

dialogue.content: ええ、できるだけそばについているのですね。
dialogue.English: I see, you're staying by her side as much as you can.

dialogue.content: はい、我が子は今の所元気なので、正直後回しになってます
dialogue.English: Yes. My child is healthy for now, so honestly, they've been taking a backseat.

dialogue.content: ただ、母に色々聞きたい事が、育児の事で、
dialogue.English: It's just that there are so many things I want to ask my mother about raising a child.

dialogue.content: そんな母が全く孫の存在に気づいていない・・・
dialogue.English: But she doesn't even seem to notice her own grandchild...

dialogue.content: ええ、今が一番、聞きたい事出てきていますよね。
dialogue.English: Yes, this is the time when you'd have the most questions for her.

dialogue.content: そこまで、お母さまは、、
dialogue.English: Your mother is in that state...

dialogue.content: はい、そうなんです。能面で、目は死んでるし、実際死にたいっていわれると
dialogue.English: Yes, that’s right. Her face is blank, her eyes look lifeless, and when she actually says she wants to die…

dialogue.content: そんな沢山の深刻な症状があるのに病名が付かないって、、
dialogue.English: To have so many serious symptoms without a clear diagnosis...

dialogue.content: あなたはお父様の態度も影響が、、とおっしゃっていましが、どういう風に影響してるとおかんがえなのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: You mentioned that your father's attitude might be having an effect... in what way do you think it's affecting her?

dialogue.content: 死にたい、って気持ちは言葉にするのは、何か心の奥にあるかもしれません、、
dialogue.English: Expressing a desire to die might indicate something deep in her heart...

dialogue.content: 父が決めつけて、起きろ！！と無理やり起こしたり、笑え！！と怒る。威圧的なのは、鬱っぽい症状の母には
dialogue.English: My father assumes things and will forcibly wake her up, shouting "Get up!!" or get angry and yell "Smile!!". His intimidating manner, for my mother who has depressive symptoms...

dialogue.content: 逆効果なんじゃないかなって
dialogue.English: I think it's probably having the opposite effect.

dialogue.content: はい、心の病気も関係してるのかなて思ったりもします
dialogue.English: Yes, I also wonder if there’s a mental health condition involved.

dialogue.content: うんうん、そのような言葉は、元気な時でも堪えると思います。
dialogue.English: Mmm, yes. Those kinds of words would be hard to hear even for someone who is well.

dialogue.content: 父に、言っても、私まで怒鳴られるし、
dialogue.English: When I say anything to my father, he ends up yelling at me too.

dialogue.content: 症状の感じだとそうも考えられるかもしれません。
dialogue.English: Given the symptoms, that could certainly be a possibility.

dialogue.content: そうですね、お父様を止めれれば一番いいですが、下手に言うより、まずはもし精神的なものがあるなら
dialogue.English: That's true. It would be best if you could stop your father, but rather than saying something that might backfire, if there is a mental health component...

dialogue.content: 父と引き離したいと実は考えてます
dialogue.English: Actually, I'm thinking of separating her from my father.

dialogue.content: ええお父様と引き離すことはできそうなのですか？
dialogue.English: I see. Is it possible to separate her from your father?

dialogue.content: あと、精神科には行かれたのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Also, has she seen a psychiatrist?

dialogue.content: はい、心療内科には、更年期症状が出だした時から通ってるので
dialogue.English: Yes, she's been going to a psychosomatic clinic since her menopausal symptoms started.

dialogue.content: そこで薬飲んで、てんかんの薬が増え、困ってるんですが、先生に言ったら言うたびに薬が増える
dialogue.English: She's been taking medication there, and they added epilepsy medication, which is worrying. But every time I mention it to the doctor, they just add more medicine.

dialogue.content: 薬をやめたいって言っても駄目なんですよね
dialogue.English: They won't let her stop the medication, even if we say we want to.

dialogue.content: 更年期症状、、区別が難しい部分もありますが、、クスリがそんなに変わっても不安になるだけですね。
dialogue.English: Menopausal symptoms... it can be difficult to distinguish, but having the medication change so much must just make you more anxious.

dialogue.content: 薬づけです
dialogue.English: She’s being overmedicated.

dialogue.content: 薬で良くなれば安心できるのに、今のままではとても心配ですね。
dialogue.English: If the medicine were helping, you could feel at ease, but as things are, it's very worrying.

dialogue.content: ここまでのお話を整理しても宜しいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Would it be alright if I summarized what we've discussed so far?

dialogue.content: はい。１日の３分の２を寝て過ごす母に薬が多すぎです。はい、お願いします
dialogue.English: Yes. There's too much medication for my mother who sleeps two-thirds of the day. Yes, please go ahead.

dialogue.content: お母さまは交通事故の後から寝たままで起きなくなり、死にたいなどと口にし手が震えたり、表情もなくなり、失禁したりする。
dialogue.English: After a car accident, your mother has been staying in bed, saying she wants to die, her hands tremble, she's become expressionless, and has episodes of incontinence.

dialogue.content: 病院で診察しても、ハッキリした病名はつかずに薬が沢山でて、それもコロコロと変わるので不安になっている。
dialogue.English: Even after seeing a doctor, there's no clear diagnosis, she's on a lot of medication that keeps changing, and this is making you anxious.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そんなお母さまに、お父様はキツイ言葉を言ってあなたはそのお父様の言動が、母に影響して鬱のような症状になっているのではと考えている。
dialogue.English: Your father says harsh things to your mother, and you believe his words and actions are affecting her, causing depressive-like symptoms.

dialogue.content: 父親と離すことも考えているということで宜しいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: And you’re considering separating her from your father, is that correct?

dialogue.content: はい、鬱j症状に関しては。はい、離して、ゆっくり療養して欲しい。薬の事も気になるけど。まだ６０歳過ぎで肌はピチピチなのに、格好や顔つきが８０歳並み。見てらんないです。
dialogue.English: Yes, regarding the depressive symptoms. Yes, I want to separate them so she can rest and recover peacefully. I'm worried about the medication too. She's only just over 60 and her skin is still so youthful, but her appearance and expression make her look like she's 80. I can't bear to watch it.

dialogue.content: ええ、辛いですよねそれだけの症状が出ているのですから何か心にダメージが影響しているのかもしれません。
dialogue.English: Yes, it must be painful. With all those symptoms, it's possible some emotional damage is affecting her.

dialogue.content: あと、気になるのが病院の処方も気になります
dialogue.English: Also, the hospital's prescriptions are a concern.

dialogue.content: 病院に関してはどうしようかと何かお考えあるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Do you have any thoughts on what to do about the hospital?

dialogue.content: はい、実は違う病院にも行ってみたんですが
dialogue.English: Yes, I actually tried going to a different hospital.

dialogue.content: ええ、
dialogue.English: Oh, you did?

dialogue.content: 相談したら、精神科のお薬って、
dialogue.English: When I asked for a consultation, they said that with psychiatric medication...

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes...

dialogue.content: 他の医者が引き継いだり、これまでの経緯とかも色々あって、受け入れたくないって
dialogue.English: ...it's difficult for another doctor to take over, given the history and everything, and that they didn't want to accept her as a patient.

dialogue.content: 断られました
dialogue.English: We were turned away.

dialogue.content: そんな、、それでは患者はどうしたらいいのか、、
dialogue.English: That can't be... what is a patient supposed to do then...?

dialogue.content: もう薬で殺されるって思い、
dialogue.English: I feel like the medications are going to kill her,

dialogue.content: 施設にショートステイ出来ないか等
dialogue.English: so I looked into things like if she could do a short stay at a facility.

dialogue.content: も聴いてみました
dialogue.English: I asked about that too.

dialogue.content: 何となく、心の状態だけではなく薬が合う合わないも考えてしまいますね、、
dialogue.English: It makes one wonder not just about her mental state, but also whether the medication is a good fit for her...

dialogue.content: ええ、それも考えられたのですね
dialogue.English: I see, you’ve considered that as well.

dialogue.content: はい、そうなんです。
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right.

dialogue.content: 年齢が若いから、在宅であと数年頑張って下さいと言われました
dialogue.English: They told me that because she's young, I should try my best to care for her at home for a few more years.

dialogue.content: そう言われると何も言えなくなってしまいますね。
dialogue.English: Hearing that leaves you at a loss for words.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: でも精神科も含めて、やはり信頼できる病院でまず見てもらうのが一番だと思いますが、、
dialogue.English: But I still think the best thing to do is to have her seen by a hospital you can trust, including a psychiatrist...

dialogue.content: あと、お母さまとはお話はできる状態なのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Also, is your mother in a state where you can talk with her?

dialogue.content: ちゃんっとした会話には繋がらないです
dialogue.English: We can’t have a proper conversation.

dialogue.content: 何度も聴いて、やっと、ぼやーんと一言返ってくるぐらいです
dialogue.English: I have to ask many times just to get a single, vague word in response.

dialogue.content: そうですか、、ご自分の事が話せたら何か解決の糸口が見つかるかと思ったのですが、、
dialogue.English: I see… I thought if she could talk about how she feels, we might find a clue toward a solution…

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: あと、かかりつけ医などにはご相談はされているのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Also, have you consulted her primary care physician?

dialogue.content: 母の、かかりつけ医が、心療内科です。くすり増える一方で止めたいんですよね。
dialogue.English: My mother's primary doctor is at the psychosomatic clinic. They just keep increasing the medicine, and I want to stop it.

dialogue.content: 繰り返し同じ事を言っていただいて申し訳ありません。
dialogue.English: I'm sorry to make you repeat yourself.

dialogue.content: いえいえ、ややこしいと思います
dialogue.English: No, no, I know it's a complicated situation.

dialogue.content: かかりつけ医が、そのような感じなのですね。
dialogue.English: So her primary physician is like that.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: やはり、もう一度、別の病院に行かれるつもりはありますか？このままでは、良くないと思います。
dialogue.English: Do you think you might try another hospital again? I don't think things can continue as they are.

dialogue.content: 何度も頼んで調べてもらっても、これ以上は、正直見当たらないですね、初老認知症で片付けられたり。写真もみせてもらって、
dialogue.English: I've asked them to check so many times, but they honestly say they can't find anything else. It gets written off as early-onset dementia. They even showed me the scans,

dialogue.content: 何もないってハンコ押されたら、意気消沈です
dialogue.English: and when they stamp it with "nothing wrong," I just feel completely dejected.

dialogue.content: それは辛いです。お母さまに何かあってからではあまりにも辛いので、何とか解決法を探したいですね。
dialogue.English: That is painful. It would be too devastating if something happened to your mother, so we really want to find a solution.

dialogue.content: はい、いつ倒れるか分からないので。
dialogue.English: Yes, because we don’t know when she might collapse.

dialogue.content: はい、死にたいとかの発言されるのもとても心配になります。
dialogue.English: Yes, and her saying she wants to die is also extremely worrying.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 色々混じってるのかなとも思ったり
dialogue.English: I sometimes think it might be a mix of different things.

dialogue.content: どちらにしても、鬱のような時は脳がとても疲れていますから、まず、しっかり睡眠をとって、
dialogue.English: In any case, when someone is in a depressive state, their brain is very tired, so the first thing is to get plenty of sleep,

dialogue.content: 落ち着ける場所でしっかり休むことが必要だと思います。
dialogue.English: and I think it's necessary to rest well in a calm environment.

dialogue.content: はい、睡眠は怖いくらい寝ます。環境と薬を整えたいと願ってます
dialogue.English: Yes, she sleeps a frightening amount. I hope we can sort out her environment and medication.

dialogue.content: 素人考えですが
dialogue.English: It's just a layman's opinion, though.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I understand.

dialogue.content: 鬱のような時はとにかく眠いようですから。
dialogue.English: It seems that when one is in a depressive state, they feel very sleepy.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: あなたが、お母さまの傍で環境を整えて見守ってあげたら、お母さまも安心されると思います。
dialogue.English: If you are by her side, creating a calm environment and watching over her, I think your mother will feel more at ease.

dialogue.content: 数年経って施設へショートでも利用できるようになれば、施設の主治医もいるので
dialogue.English: In a few years, if she becomes eligible for short stays at a facility, they have a facility doctor there, so...

dialogue.content: そこまでなんとか、って思ったりもしています
dialogue.English: I sometimes think if we can just make it until then.

dialogue.content: 数年も我慢するのはあなたもお母さまも辛いですね。
dialogue.English: Enduring this for several more years must be difficult for both you and your mother.

dialogue.content: 父さえ、穏やかになってくれれば
dialogue.English: If only my father could become calmer…

dialogue.content: こういう場合どこに相談したらいいのか、私の方からは案がなく申し訳ないです。
dialogue.English: I'm very sorry, but I don't have a suggestion for where to turn for advice in a case like this.

dialogue.content: ええ、お父様の事も気がかりです。
dialogue.English: Yes, your father is also a concern.

dialogue.content: いえ、とんでもないです。聞いてもらっただけでも、随分楽になりました
dialogue.English: No, not at all. Just having you listen has made me feel much lighter.

dialogue.content: （時間が過ぎてしまいました。提案まで行ききれず、、解決法が浮かびませんでした）
dialogue.English: (We have run over time. I wasn’t able to get to concrete suggestions, and I couldn’t come up with a solution.)

dialogue.content: いえ、大丈夫です
dialogue.English: No, it's okay.

dialogue.content: 少しでも気が楽になっていただけたのならそれは嬉しいです。
dialogue.English: I'm glad if you feel even a little bit better.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: こういう精神科の件は、何か方法があるかもしれないので今回は私の宿題にさせていただけますでしょうか？
dialogue.English: There may be some way forward regarding psychiatry in cases like this; may I take this as my homework to look into?

dialogue.content: はい、ありがとうございます。また、よ是非ろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you. I would appreciate that very much.

dialogue.content: 何か方法がないか、調べてまたお伝えさせていた抱けたらと思います。
dialogue.English: I would like to look into what options there might be and let you know.

dialogue.content: 是非、宜しくお願い致します。↑です
dialogue.English: Yes, please. I look forward to it.

dialogue.content: はい、少しでも楽になれたとのこと、良かったです。また、引き続きよろしくお願いいたします。
dialogue.English: Yes, I'm glad to hear you feel a little better. I look forward to our next session.

dialogue.content: 今日はありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you for today.

dialogue.content: こちらこそありがとうございました。では、本日は以上で終了してもよろしいでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Thank you as well. Shall we end today's session here?

dialogue.content: はい、大丈夫です
dialogue.English: Yes, that’s fine.

dialogue.content: お母さまのお体がお元気になること、あなたが安心して過ごせますように願っています。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: I hope that your mother's health improves and that you can live with more peace of mind. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: （時間オーバーして申し訳ありませんでした。コメントで改善点などよろしくお願いいたします）
dialogue.English: (I apologize for going over time. Please feel free to share any suggestions for improvement in the comments.)

dialogue.content: （今日はありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for today.)

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you as well.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました。では終了ボタン押しますね。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I’ll press the end button now.

dialogue.content: はい、お願いします
dialogue.English: Yes, please.
